AI chips ($AMD, $AVGO): $AMD is today's most widely backed stock. On the news front, CEO Lisa Su said demand still exceeds supply and plans to "significantly increase" supply in 2027, while memory overall remains tight. @LIWEI_TWCapital (original post · 10/6) added, citing the Liberty Times and TrendForce, that AMD's capacity talks with suppliers have been extended from one to two years to three to five years; he believes wafers, packaging and substrates must expand together, and a shortfall in any link would limit the ramp, so he named the capacity of $TSM and $ASX as key. @PhotonCap (original post · 10/6) believes the expansion reflects management's confidence in demand. The other three bullish accounts were mainly reviewing their track records: @asianinvestors (original post · 10/6) said he called AMD a "must-own stock" and it is up more than 200% at $630; @dannycheng2022 (original post · 10/6) said he accumulated from about $110 and the position is up nearly 6x; @firstadopter (original post · 10/6) said he was bullish during the after-hours plunge following August earnings, and it is up 36% since. The only neutral account is @amitisinvesting, who simply listed AMD as one of the big tech stocks lifting the index.

$AVGO: @TheBigBerbowski (original post · 10/6) said it is "still cheap": at about $353, the P/E is 18.3x fiscal 2027 and 11.6x fiscal 2028; last quarter's AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion rose 221% year over year, and management expects $21.7 billion in Q4; he dislikes the top five customers making up 55% of revenue and AI hardware dragging down gross margin, but thinks the valuation will become more attractive if cloud providers' AI spending continues. @jpinsights (original post · 10/6) discussed the financing risk of the Anthropic deal: banks have started syndicating $60 billion of financing, $42 billion of which is senior debt backed by Broadcom's A- credit and $18 billion is subordinated debt without a Broadcom guarantee, with Blackstone having taken $9 billion; he still wants to see how smoothly the $42 billion placement goes, but if it goes well, this concern would ease significantly. @asianinvestors asked why the forward P/E is only 21x, and @ripster47's long-term portfolio also holds AVGO.

Marvell investor day ($MRVL): News accounts reported CEO Matt Murphy said the 2030 addressable market is about $400 billion, with fiscal 2028 revenue of about $20 billion and fiscal 2031 revenue of $70–90 billion; the stock turned from a premarket loss to a gain, at one point up 9.1%, its highest since June 30. The 3 bullish accounts are @PhotonBull (original post · 10/6), who said the stock reacted very positively to the CEO's comments; @asianinvestors (original post · 10/6), who said it is up about 45% since he recommended it at about $205 two months ago; and @LIWEI_TWCapital, who posted a screenshot of the stock up 8.52% on the day. It is a large cap (the screenshot shows a market cap of about $259.1 billion).

Tonight's update: @TheValueist (original post · 10/6) cited Barron's midday report: Marvell's fiscal 2031 revenue target is $70–90 billion, versus $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026, implying about 55–60% annual growth; at the midpoint, custom chips are $30 billion and interconnect $37.5 billion, and it mentioned a cumulative $120 billion deal with Google; the stock rose 7.2% to $290.82. He said the bar was extremely high but it was cleared, and $70–90 billion will become the new bull baseline, with the debate shifting to execution and custom chip share versus Broadcom; he also noted that RBC's prior estimate of fiscal 2029 AI revenue of "more than $10 billion plus $2 billion" was not confirmed by the midday report. @damnang2 (original post · 10/6) celebrated with a screenshot of $MRVL at $289.36, up 6.67% on the day. So $MRVL now has 5 bullish accounts and no bearish ones.

Memory ($MU, $SNDK): The conclusions from the first batch of data still hold. @ren_stocks (original post · 10/6) became more bullish after reading a JPMorgan report: Micron's long-term supply agreements rose from 16 to 26 within one quarter, prepayments rose from $22 billion to $32 billion, about 75% of 2027 output is locked in, and 2027 HBM is sold out with prices up 54% year over year. @vikramskr (original post · 10/6) cited a BofA report saying it does not believe in HBM "spec downgrades", though BofA also expects average memory selling prices to fall about 10% in 2028. @aleabitoreddit picked $SNDK as a winning pick, so SNDK has 3 bullish accounts. New: @damnang2 (original post · 10/6) said HBM4 supply is very unstable: one memory maker paused 8-high sample shipments because of another's situation, and customers are wavering between 8-high and 12-high; in short, HBM is scarce and suppliers can set their own prices, but production is extremely difficult (no stocks named). @pequityresearch also cited UBS saying memory makes up 68% of the bill of materials for Nvidia's VR200.

Other consensus bullish:

  • $NBIS: @pequityresearch (original post · 10/6) cited William Blair forecasting Nebius ARR growing from $1.25 billion in fiscal 2025 to $71.7 billion in fiscal 2030; @asianinvestors and @ripster47 also listed it as a win/holding. Tonight @ren_stocks (original post · 10/6) posted a screenshot of $NBIS at $252.43, up 8.54% on the day; @dannycheng2022 (original post · 10/6) said he added more on pullbacks over the past month, having previously bought at $96 last year and below $180 this August, per the post. 5 bullish accounts in total.
  • $TSM (ADR): @pequityresearch (original post · 10/6) cited experts saying 2nm monthly capacity will exceed 120,000 wafers by end of 2027 (consensus 110,000), and advanced packaging capacity will grow 70–80% year over year in 2027–28; @dannycheng2022 has been bullish since building a position in February 2024; @LIWEI_TWCapital sees it as key to AMD's expansion.
  • $VST: The US Department of Energy is preparing $4.0–4.2 billion in loans to upgrade three nuclear plants. @TheValueist (original post · 10/6) said $CEG $VST $TLN $NRG, a group of power stocks that have lagged for 18 months, could catch up; @cmsinvests ranked VST first among nuclear beneficiaries; @PhotonBull joked that Thiel and Pelosi have both bought, classified as neutral.
  • $BRUN: Boost Run signed a five-year $525.6 million contract with a sovereign AI company, bringing total cumulative contract value to over $2.6 billion; @asianinvestors said it was up more than 10% premarket, and @athuinvests (original post · 10/6) believes it is extremely undervalued on forward metrics.
  • $AAOI: @EhrmantrautCap_ (original post · 10/6) added on September 28 at $96.20, now $128 today; plus @aleabitoreddit's conditional bullish view that "it beats $LITE if there's no more dilution". $LITE has two accounts, both neutral.
  • $CRDO: @asianinvestors and @ripster47 listed as a win/holding (ripster's portfolio has unrealized gains of about 48%).
  • $CEG, $VST (nuclear): @MMatters22596 (original post · 10/6) said it is no coincidence that $CEG rose more than 10% today: $GOOGL signed a 20-year, 3.59GW power agreement, including upgrades to 11 reactors adding 890MW of new nuclear capacity and unlocking $4.3 billion of investment, raising CEG's nuclear capacity by about 4%; his medium-term target is $635–$702, provided $228.63 holds, and a break below it would invalidate this view. @cmsinvests (original post · 10/6) said he called $VST $135, $CEG $250 a few days ago, with a chart showing VST at $159.79 (+10.27% on the day) and CEG at $304.01 (+13.60%), and is now calling $IREN $42 and $CRWV $90 (small cap (market cap < $50B)), but did not mention targets or stop losses.
  • $QCOM: @michaelsikand (original post · 10/6) interviewed Qualcomm CFO Akash Palkhiwala, focusing on the roadmap for the data center business from 0 to $15 billion (customers include $META, $AMZN), wearables possibly bringing growth not priced into the stock, and Qualcomm "taking the lead" in humanoid robots; his partner @KawzInvests (original post · 10/6) added that the memory shortage clouds the near-term outlook, but data center CPUs and robotics could rewrite the growth story. Video content not reviewed.
  • $NVDA, $PLTR: @dannycheng2022 (original post · 10/6) said two years ago he told his group not to go heavy on $CLSK, $MARA, $RIOT (which he saw as "lottery tickets", bearish), and to buy NVDA at about $70 and PLTR at about $20 instead, held throughout for about 3.5x and 9x respectively; in another post (original post · 10/6) he said this year's most expensive mistake was listening to bears and selling $AMD, $PLTR, $NVDA.
  • $ASTS: @MMatters22596 (original post · 10/6) said it broke out of a wedge on heavy volume and is coming out of a base, but needs to clear the prior high to confirm, after which the target is $100–$120 (small cap (market cap < $50B)). In addition, @PhotonBull is neutral.

Split: No stock today has both bullish and bearish accounts. New cautious voices tonight: @firstadopter (original post · 10/6) said "sentiment is starting to overheat, be careful"; @HatedMoats (original post · 10/6) posted a screenshot of $NVO at $36.98, down 1.49%, asking "has it become a joke", a short-term bearish view. $MSFT has only @HatedMoats (original post · 10/6) quoting Jim Cramer's "the big MSFT rally is coming" with a mocking GIF, classified as leaning bearish, while the other two accounts are neutral. $NVDA hit a record high; @jpinsights said it is still undervalued and @dannycheng2022 is also bullish, with the other three neutral; among them, @KobeissiLetter (original post · 10/6) pointed out that Nvidia makes up 5.21% of the MSCI World Index, near a record high, more than double its 2024 weight, larger than Japan's 5.16%, and more than twice Germany's 1.79%, France's 1.93% and China's 2.31%, stating only facts with no bullish or bearish stance. @amitisinvesting (original post · 10/6) warned: the index's record highs rely mainly on big tech, with financials, consumer discretionary and even memory stocks not participating; oil prices have risen sharply this year and bond yields remain at three-year highs, so the market could be a bull trap, or it could be pricing in a pullback in yields and oil and a much lower chance of rate hikes.

Macro read (bonds and breadth): The S&P 500 hit a record high today, and @KobeissiLetter said its market cap reached $71.3 trillion. But bond market pressure has not eased: @KobeissiLetter (original post · 10/6) said spreads on CCC-rated and lower corporate bonds rose to 12.0%, the widest since November 2022, up a sharp 298 basis points in five months; the 10-year Treasury earlier topped 5.30% and the 30-year topped 5.60%, and fixed income ETFs' share of trading rose to 27%. JPMorgan CEO Dimon said inflation is sticky and rates may rise further. @NickTimiraos (original post · 10/6) said after remarks from two Fed vice chairs, the probability of an October rate hike fell from about 70% to about 25%. @LizAnnSonders noted the September ISM services prices paid rose to the highest since July 2022, and @KevRGordon believes core PCE services inflation could rise again; the US August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, with semiconductor imports up 185% year over year. @kevinxu said yields have peaked and to get ready for "Uptober". In Europe, Bank of France Governor Moulin warned that without fiscal action France risks being "strangled" by interest rates, and @firstadopter cited The Wall Street Journal saying the Iran war has pushed up rates, with France hit hardest. On oil, US Energy Secretary Wright said diesel prices peaked a few weeks ago; the IEA expects to decide details of the G7's 100 million barrel release on October 14–15.

@LizAnnSonders (original post · 10/6) posted Schwab and Bloomberg breadth data as of 10/5 tonight, explaining why record index highs do not mean every stock is rising: the S&P 500 is up 14% year to date with a maximum index drawdown of only -9%, but the average maximum drawdown of its members is -26%; the Nasdaq is up 18% with a -13% drawdown, while its members average a -45% drawdown; the Russell 2000 is up 15%, with members at -36%. Over the past 1 month, only 19% of S&P members outperformed the index (only 9% over 1 year). Another set of his charts (original post · 10/6) shows only about 28% of S&P members above their 50-day line and about 48% above their 200-day line, with tech strongest at about 76% and utilities, real estate and consumer staples weakest; however, he also said (original post · 10/6) more sectors are hitting 4-week highs, and "more sectors are finally showing signs of life". Big tech performance (original post · 10/6): $MU is up 272.8% year to date, ranking 1st in contribution to the S&P, $NVDA +28.1%, $AAPL +22.4%, while $AVGO is only +4.7% and $TSLA -15.8%. The implication is that gains are concentrated in a few stocks, consistent with @amitisinvesting's breadth warning. @RaoulGMI (original post · 10/6) reposted a partnership between Mysten Labs and Google Cloud using the Sui blockchain to record evidence of AI agent behavior, calling it "a big deal, badly needed", with no mention of US stocks.

Big names (Trump, Musk): Elon Musk only reposted a video of @mattyp hooking Grok Bot up to a printer tonight (original post · 10/6); video content not reviewed, no stocks mentioned. @realDonaldTrump made 15 posts on Truth Social (mostly election endorsements and attacks on the media), four of which were market related:

  • Medical device tariffs (original post · 10/6): he said Becton Dickinson ($BDX, small cap (market cap < $50B)) agreed to invest $3 billion to move production of syringes, needles and test kits back to the US, with more than $1 billion of that in Nebraska, and said the reason is his medical device tariffs, to take effect before year end.
  • Cash payments (original post · 10/6): he said if Republicans win both chambers of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, every adult citizen would receive $5,000, without mentioning funding or timing. However, Kalshi markets show a 92% probability of Democrats controlling the House and 64% for the Senate.
  • Oil prices (original post · 10/6): he said what is pushing up gasoline prices is no longer the Strait of Hormuz, but bombed Russian refineries, plus refinery closures in states such as California.
  • The New York Times (original post · 10/6): he posted several times attacking the NYT ($NYT, small cap (market cap < $50B)) for altered images and false reporting, saying its subscriptions have plunged, without providing data.

Market news (headlines only, not counted toward consensus): Here are tonight's key headlines from news accounts (Hong Kong time):

  • 20:30: US August trade deficit of $105.6 billion, vs. about $102.0 billion expected; imports rose 4.3% and exports rose 1.4% (reported by DeItaone, FirstSquawk and financialjuice).
  • 20:15: ADP data show private payrolls added an average of 23,750 per week in the 4 weeks to September 19 (confirmed by several news accounts).
  • 20:16: CrowdStrike, AWS and Nvidia expanded a cybersecurity startup accelerator program, involving $CRWD, $NVDA (confirmed by several sources).
  • 20:09: Uber ($UBER) is buying ezCater for $2.3 billion in cash; 19:38: Energy Transfer ($ET) is acquiring Vaquero Midstream for $2.625 billion; 21:00: Applied Materials ($AMAT) and Intel ($INTC) are partnering on AI chip technology R&D.
  • 20:28: Iran said the Strait of Hormuz will not open under threats or pressure (DeItaone, confirmed by FirstSquawk); 20:15: UK Maritime Trade Operations received a report that a tanker leaving Hormuz was struck by an unknown object.
  • 21:14–21:19: JPMorgan CEO Dimon said inflation may stay sticky and rates may go higher, and said cyber risk has risen 10x since Anthropic launched Mythos; Energy Secretary Wright said Hormuz is still a conflict zone, so oil is near $100, but diesel prices may have peaked.
  • 22:45: StockMKTNewz relayed Michael Burry saying the stock market is in a "denial" phase, which, based on 2000 and 2008, could last 6–9 months.
  • 22:49–22:50: American Century said a 5.25% 10-year yield is attractive, market expectations of 4 rate hikes in a year are too aggressive, and cracks are appearing in CCC-rated debt; 20:02: UBS said this bond selloff is not a repeat of 1999, because the deficit exceeds 6% of GDP (both from DeItaone, not confirmed by a second source).
  • 23:05–23:10: Bank of Japan board member Sato supports gradual rate hikes but is worried about weak consumption (DeItaone, confirmed by LiveSquawk); Russia's Volgograd refinery (about 5% of Russian refining capacity) halted output after a drone attack on 10/2 (confirmed by financialjuice).

Worth watching: AI subscription costs remain a topic. @insane_analyst (original post · 10/6) posted a chart showing that for the same $200 monthly fee at API prices, ChatGPT Pro is worth about $2,084 (10.4x) and Claude Max 20x about $11,726 (58.6x), questioning whether ARR would still grow as fast without subsidies, leaning bearish. In contrast, @firstadopter posted Claude's "currently too busy" screen, saying compute is still in short supply, and pushed back on BofA's claim that "the era of easy AI money is over". In optical communications, @LIWEI_TWCapital (original post · 10/6) cited a Taiwan National Science and Technology Council CPO program document saying testing can account for 20–30% of module cost, and the only two US companies shown for test equipment are $TER and $KEYS, both of which he is bullish on.

Earnings dates: $PENG reports after the US close on 10/6 (early morning 10/7 Hong Kong time), and @TheBigBerbowski said to watch gross margin (implied about 26%) and fiscal 2027 guidance; $SNDK reports after the US close on 10/29 (confirmed by the company); $LITE reports after the US close on 11/5 (confirmed by the company); $AAOI is estimated for 11/5 as well, but the company has not officially announced it; $NVDA reports after the close on 11/25, per a screenshot.

Of 353 posts, 73 had a clear bullish or bearish stance (63 bullish, 10 bearish); the 17 consensus bullish stocks involve 22 accounts.

Content comes from public posts by tracked accounts; not investment advice.

  • $PEP 3: @leadlagreport (original post, 10/9) noted that 4 points of the 3% rise in core operating profit came from tariff refunds, so excluding them it declined; @carlquintanilla shared that North American volumes have fallen for 16 straight quarters while prices rise 7% a year; @TheStalwart shared a view that Pepsi, unlike Nike, cannot blame the weakness on execution missteps.

  • $SBUX 1 bullish, 2 bearish: Starbucks is exploring an acquisition of Chipotle. @Stephanie_Link thinks the stock's drop of as much as 6% creates an opportunity; @garyblack00 shared FT Lex saying synergies are limited and the after-tax return is only 6%; @firstadopter said bluntly it makes no sense at all.

@saylor keeps promoting tokenized shares of $MSTR and $STRC; @SawyerMerritt said Tesla Robotaxi drove well even in heavy rain at night, and @StockSavvyShay cited Lemonade's insurance discount for FSD miles as support. Period covered: 2026-10-05 08:31 to 2026-10-06 18:19 HKT. 17 posts in total, 7 of them with a ticker.
Team scope: US common stocks, market cap ≥ $50B, cash long positions only, no ETFs.

This version (redone at 19:30 HKT): every post was pulled through fxtwitter for the full text, quoted posts and attached images, and every image was checked. Posts with a stance rose from 5 to 7; posts with stance_by_ticker rose from 4 to 5.

First: team holdings and the October Top10

  • Holdings (BE, INTC, TER, AMAT, MRVL): of today's 17 posts, not a single one mentioned them, either explicitly or implicitly. No bearish views and no hard risks.
  • The only Top10 names mentioned were $MU and $LITE: WDC, DELL, AMD, COHR and MRNA were not mentioned at all. INTC, TER and MRVL, as above, were not mentioned.
  • 　$MU: two bullish posts (@ren_stocks, @vikramskr), nobody bearish. But note the following risks (detailed below):
  • 　BofA forecasts memory ASPs will fall about 10% in 2028 (DRAM down 5%, NAND down 13%). BofA calls this a "soft landing", with prices rising again only in 2029 to 30.
  • 　Market cap is already up about 274% year to date.
  • 　$LITE: neutral. @aleabitoreddit only used it as a comparison, saying AAOI will outperform LITE. That is a relatively weaker view, but it is not bearish on LITE itself, and it is not a reason to go long either.
  • 　Optical communications sector background (no ticker): @PhotonCap discussed the Hybrid PIC market with a neutral stance. Data center optical interconnect is the main growth driver, relevant to LITE and COHR. However, he pointed out the report's CAGR was overstated: 13.6% should actually be 10.8%.

By ticker

$MU (Micron): in scope ✅ (market cap about $1.20T), a Top10 name
  • @ren_stocks: bullish | fundamentals | long term
  • 　Figures only visible in the full text (citing JPM's Memory Market Update; attached images checked):
  • 　Micron expects supply in 2027 and 2028 to be tighter than in 2026, with "no visibility on when supply and demand will balance", because of a shortage of cleanroom space.
  • 　Long-term supply agreements rose from 16 to 26 within one quarter, with order visibility out to 2031.
  • 　Prepayments rose from $22B to $32B, contract backlog is $150B, and about 75% of 2027 output is already locked in.
  • 　HBM for 2027 is already sold out, with prices up 54% year over year. HBM bit demand is growing 63%, versus 37% for other server memory.
  • 　In his words: "Memory bears are running out of years to be right."
  • 　A JPM detail in the attached image: MU has locked in roughly 35%+ of revenue through 2030 via SCAs, while LTA coverage at Asian peers exceeds 50%. JPM considers MU's figure conservative.
  • 　Link: Original post ↗
  • @vikramskr: bullish | fundamentals | long term (this time upgraded from "indirect support" to a formal stance; the view is in the attached image)
  • 　The post itself is just one line: "BoA never bought into this despec rumor", quoting @damnang2 saying HBM4 will go from 8Hi back to 12Hi.
  • 　The real content is in the attached image, which is BofA's September 19 Global Memory Tech report:
  • 　The report says outright that it does not expect new GPUs/ASICs to "de-spec". Instead, it expects memory per chip to keep rising: Rubin Ultra uses 1,000GB, the new Rubin 384GB, versus 288GB today.
  • 　The 2030 DRAM + NAND market (TAM) was raised to $2.0tn (previously $1.8tn); the report calls it an "L-T super-cycle".
  • 　2027 to 28 DRAM/NAND ASP assumptions were raised 8–12%/2–3%.
  • 　⚠️ Hard risk (same image): BofA expects ASPs to fall about 10% in 2028 (DRAM down 5%, NAND down 13%), and revenue growth in 2028 to slow sharply (DRAM from +60% in 2027 to +12%, NAND from +33% to +3%).
  • 　Link: Original post ↗
$SNDK (Sandisk): in scope ✅ (market cap about $250B)
  • @ren_stocks: bullish | fundamentals | long term. Same reasoning as above, from the same JPM memory report.
  • @vikramskr: bullish. The BofA image states "NAND upside also emerging", with Q3 NAND prices up more than 15% quarter over quarter. However, the post is about HBM, so its support for SNDK is more indirect.
  • @aleabitoreddit: bullish, in passing. In the older post he quoted, he listed $SNDK and Samsung as names "already making money now", to contrast with the opportunity cost of AAOI's repeated share issuance. This is only visible in the quoted post.
  • Risks:
  • 　BofA expects NAND ASPs to fall 13% in 2028.
  • 　Verified: market cap is up more than 12x in a year, 52-week high $2,354.39, recent close about $1,704–1,720, very volatile.
$LITE (Lumentum): in scope ✅ (market cap about $97.9B), a Top10 name
